children: Democratic lawmakers, led by Sen.
Elizabeth Warren
(D-Mass.), urged the SEC Chair
Paul Atkins
on Wednesday to abandon proposed cryptocurrency rules they say could create loopholes and weaken investor protections.
Warren and Allies Demand Answers
In the first letter, led by Warren and joined by Sen.
Chris Van Hollen
(D-Md.) and Sen.
Tina Smith
(D-Minn.), the lawmakers argued that the proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets" rule would allow cryptocurrency assets to escape the SEC’s regulatory regime and give them “special treatment.”
Critics also argued the proposal stops states from enforcing their own cryptocurrency laws and weakens long-standing Supreme Court precedent on how SEC jurisdiction is decided.
“The proposal would create a new ‘tailored securities offering regime’ for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets," the senators wrote.
In the second letter, led by Hollen, the lawmakers urged the SEC to reverse its September decision
and certain liquidity providers from federal securities rules.
The senators said the order would let platforms that trade tokenized stocks avoid long-standing market rules and create new risks for investors and publicly traded companies.
Cryptocurrency Oversight to Tighten in 2027?
The dispute follows the SEC’s broader effort to establish clearer cryptocurrency rules.
Last month, Atkins said the

params.linkText: market had grown from a "niche curiosity into a multi-trillion-dollar asset class,"

children: while adding regulation had failed to keep pace.
The SEC Chair said the new rules would replace the "grey of uncertainty" created by rules of a "bygone era."
Warren’s influence over cryptocurrency policy could expand next year. A report said she is expected to become Chair of the Senate Banking Committee in 2027,

params.linkText: potentially giving her subpoena authority to examine cryptocurrency companies’ consumer-protection practices

children: and alleged misconduct involving prediction markets.
